title: A full Karger run terminates with two vertices
statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be multigraphs on a common vertex type, and suppose $G$ has at least two vertices. If $H$ is obtained from $G$ by a graph-only Karger run consisting of exactly $n - 2$ successive edge-occurrence contractions, where $n$ is the number of vertices of $G$, then $H$ has exactly two vertices.
hypotheses_covered: G and H are multigraphs on the same vertex type
G has at least two vertices
H is reachable from G by a Karger run of length (number of vertices of G) − 2
replaced:
If $G$ has at least two vertices and $H$ is reachable from $G$ by
$G.\mathrm{vertexCount} - 2$ contractions, then $H$ has exactly two vertices.
